Here is the input problem:
  Axiom 1 (flattening): op2 = op(x2, x2).
  Axiom 2 (flattening): op3 = op(x1, op(x2, x2)).
  Axiom 3 (flattening): op4 = op(x0, op(x1, op(x2, x2))).
  Axiom 4 (a1): X = op(X, op(op(X, op(X, Y)), Z)).
  Axiom 5 (flattening): op5 = op(x0, op(x0, op(x1, op(x2, x2)))).
  Goal 1 (conjecture0): x0 = op(x0, op(x0, op(x1, op(x2, x2)))).

(13.0) 1. op(x2, x2) -> op2
(13.0) 2. op(x1, op2) -> op3
(13.0) 3. op(x0, op3) -> op4

The conjecture is true! Here is a proof.

Axiom 1 (a1): X = op(X, op(op(X, op(X, Y)), Z)).

Lemma 2: op(X, op(X, op(X, Y))) = X.
Proof:
  op(X, op(X, op(X, Y)))
= { by axiom 1 (a1) }
  op(X, op(op(X, op(X, Y)), op(op(op(X, op(X, Y)), op(op(X, op(X, Y)), Z)), W))) (peak)
= { by axiom 1 (a1) R->L }
  X

Lemma 3: op(X, op(X, Y)) = X.
Proof:
  op(X, op(X, Y))
= { by lemma 2 R->L }
  op(X, op(op(X, op(X, op(X, Z))), Y)) (peak)
= { by axiom 1 (a1) R->L }
  X

Goal 1 (conjecture0): x0 = op(x0, op(x0, op(x1, op(x2, x2)))).
Proof:
  x0
= { by lemma 3 R->L }
  op(x0, op(x0, op(x1, op(x2, x2)))) (peak)

RESULT: Theorem (the conjecture is true).
